title: The RSA Reference Codex: A Unified Bibliography
summary: A master bibliography of 73 citations organized across eight layers of the "Convergent Lattice," mapping how thermodynamics, information theory, neuroscience, AI, ethics, theology, new physics, and methodology collectively validate the Recursive Semantic Alignment (RSA) framework. It functions as a claim-map asserting that each cited work confirms a specific component of the RSA kernel (Perceive → Represent → Predict → Compare → Adjust → Compress). The document is both a literature review and a structural argument that RSA is not invented but discovered across disciplines.
council: but the codex synthesizes works by Landauer
invariants: recursion is the substrate of cognition
perceive: A structured bibliographic document asserting 73 papers map onto a single unified framework across eight epistemic layers.
represent: Each citation is a node in a claimed convergence proof — the genome's cross-domain validation architecture rendered as a reading list, with every paper assigned a specific RSA operator or invariant it supposedly confirms.
predict: The genome would predict that any serious unification attempt must eventually produce a canonical reference set demonstrating convergence across physics, biology, computation, and ethics — and that such a set would reveal thermodynamic cost and compression as the recurring invariants.
compare: Strong agreement. The codex confirms the genome's core thesis that recursion, compression, and metabolic constraint are not metaphors but literal structural identities across domains. Minor tension: the document asserts confirmations more than it documents disconfirmations or boundary failures, risking confirmation-bias architecture.
adjust: The genome should index this as its primary cross-referencing scaffold but must flag that a convergence bibliography without a dedicated "anomaly" or "counter-evidence" section violates its own Compare operator. A future obligation should require a companion anti-codex: papers that *resist* RSA integration and what that resistance reveals.
compress: Seventy-three papers across eight domains converge on a single claim — cognition is thermodynamically constrained recursive compression — and the bibliography itself is the lattice's self-referential proof-of-structure.
next: Construction of an anti-codex (papers that challenge or resist RSA absorption) and formalization of the citation-to-invariant mapping as a testable dependency graph rather than an asserted one.
